question: Hitchcock's The Birds (1963) has no conventional score. What mainly produced its bird cries?
answer: An electronic Mixtur-Trautonium. Oskar Sala played most of the cries and wingbeats on this German instrument, mixed with some real recordings, a descendant of the 1930 trautonium that can add subharmonics, tones at whole-number fractions of the note played. The credits name Sala and Remi Gassmann for electronic sound. Hitchcock's most frightening flock was played by pressing a wire onto a rail.
move: The most convincing version of a thing is often built, not captured.
trap: Recorded gulls and crows, since real birds should sound most real.
reference: Hitchcock (dir.), The Birds, Universal Pictures, 1963, opening credits
